subject: Pilot specs & model recommendations — streaming behavior recap

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot specs & model recommendations — streaming behavior recap

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a short pilot targeting the streaming UX issues you showed (partial outputs & stop-sequence behavior).

Call highlights:
- Primary goal: Replace rule-based summarization in the live notes feature with a streaming LLM that emits coherent partial summaries as the call progresses.
- Pain points you demoed: truncated sentences mid-output when agent hit stop tokens, occasional hallucinated clause at the end of partial outputs, and tail latency spikes when multiple agents stream concurrently.
- SLO targets you quoted: < 300ms 95th percentile per-token tail; end-to-end visible partial update within 400ms.

What we recommend for the pilot (high level):
1) Two model variants to evaluate in parallel: Redwood-Edge-13B (quantized, low-latency) + Redwood-XL-34B (higher-quality fallback for longer context).
2) Evaluation artifacts: we attached a representative prompt set (pilot_prompt_set_v1.json) and a short benchmark harness we usually run for streaming (sample results attached).
3) Metrics to capture: partial-output coherence (human-rated), stop-sequence correctness, per-token tail latency (p50/p95/p99), and token cost/throughput.
4) Duration & scope: 2-week technical pilot with a 24/7 window of synthetic traffic + 3 shadowed real sessions from your team.

Action items I propose:
- Michael: spin up a scoped pilot infra and share benchmark link + simple dashboard.
- Neha: run initial evals on requested prompt set and surface any quality regressions to Alicia.
- Alicia/Tom: confirm the 3 sample sessions (dates) and share any additional prompt variants you want in the set.

Attachments: pilot_prompt_set_v1.json (prompt examples + stop-token context), streaming_benchmark_results_sample.csv (sample latency/coherence rows), pilot_scope_template.docx

If that looks good, we can lock in a kickoff next Monday (6/21) for the technical deep dive.

Best,
Michael Grant
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Michael — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side after showing the product team: 

1) The partial-output problem: see snippet below from yesterday's session (we redacted PHI):

--- begin snippet ---
Agent: "Here's the recommended follow-up: schedule an in-person visit for the patient to..."
(then the stream paused and the UI showed: "for the patient to")
--- end snippet ---

So the visible partial output ended abruptly; when the model completed the sentence the UI didn't patch the partial chunk correctly and users assumed the sentence was finished. We need partial chunks to be coherent (not cut mid-clause) and for stop sequences to behave predictably across reconnections.

2) Latency: the 300ms target is firm for p95. If you have internal latency profiles for the two suggested model variants that would help.

3) Security: we'll need a short SOC2 evidence pack and confirmation on data retention for pilot logs (30 days).

We confirm the 3 shadow sessions on 6/22 at 10:00, 6/23 at 14:30, and 6/24 at 09:15 PT. Please include the prompt set and also the exact benchmark harness definition so our engineers can reproduce locally.

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Ramos
Product Lead, LiveNotes

Subject: Fwd: Pilot specs & model recommendations — streaming behavior recap

Team — forwarding Alicia's asks. Quick tech plan and what I need from you both before Friday: 

Summary of asks from MediCor:
- p95 per-token tail latency < 300ms under modest concurrency (3-5 concurrent streams).
- Partial-output coherence: avoid mid-clause cutoffs; prefer model-side heuristics + client-side reassembly.
- Deterministic stop-token behavior on reconnects.
- SOC2 evidence + 30-day log retention for pilot.

Proposed tests to run (Neha):
- Run the pilot_prompt_set_v1.json through our streaming harness at both model sizes and three quantization modes (8-bit, 4-bit-int8, and int4 experimental) and produce CSVs with p50/p95/p99 per-token tail latency + per-example stop-token correctness flag. Put results in the Drive link and attach a short README of the harness steps.
- Produce a short human-rating test (10 control prompts) focusing on partial coherence (Likert 1-5).

Operational plan (Marcus):
- Configure an A/B routing policy in the sandbox cluster: 60% Redwood-Edge-13B-quant (low-latency) / 40% Redwood-XL-34B for fallback. Set timeout and circuit-breaker thresholds so if per-token tail > 600ms we instantly fallback to smaller model.
- Enable KV-prefix caching for repeated context in the pilot (we expect repeated prompt patterns).

Risks & mitigations:
- Mid-output cuts are usually a mix of stop-token misalignment + UI reassembly. Recommend we implement a client-side patching algorithm that waits up to 250ms for an extra token buffer before committing a chunk to UI. Also try model-side avoidance of training stop sequences in completions.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Neha: initial CSV + human-rating summary by EOD Friday (6/18).
- Marcus: sandbox routing + fallback config and pilot dashboard link by Monday EOD (6/21).
- Michael: send SOC2 evidence stub & pilot scope to customer and schedule kickoff (I'll take this).

Let me know if any of this is unrealistic given infra constraints.

- Michael
